walkthroughs.body_html:
World History Topics (two, same as SL) — a core area of History.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

World History Topics (two, same as SL) brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

mcqs.q: Which 1938 conference ceded the Sudetenland to Germany?
options: Locarno
Munich
Yalta
Geneva

mcqs.q: Who signed the 1939 non-aggression pact for the USSR?
options: Molotov
Litvinov
Khrushchev
Beria

mcqs.q: Why did Lenin introduce the NEP in 1921?
options: The NEP was introduced by Stalin to fund the Five-Year Plans.
The NEP was Lenin's plan to permanently switch Russia to capitalism.
War Communism had collapsed the economy and provoked the Kronstadt revolt; the NEP allowed limited private trade to restore production and stabilise Bolshevik rule.
Japan attacked to support Germany's invasion of the USSR.

mcqs.q: Why did Japan attack Pearl Harbor?
options: Japan attacked to support Germany's invasion of the USSR.
The NEP was introduced by Stalin to fund the Five-Year Plans.
To cripple the US Pacific Fleet and buy time to secure resource-rich Southeast Asia after the US oil embargo threatened Japanese expansion.
Japan attacked because it wanted to conquer America.

mcqs.q: Why did Huguenots migrate to England from the 1680s?
options: The NEP was introduced by Stalin to fund the Five-Year Plans.
Huguenots came to England because France was poorer than England.
Louis XIV's 1685 revocation of the Edict of Nantes ended toleration of French Protestants; many fled persecution to Protestant England, bringing skills like silk weaving.
Huguenots were Catholic refugees fleeing Cromwell.
